subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should configured OpenAI-compatible memory embedding endpoints inherit the shared three-state `request.allowPrivateNetwork` contract: exact configured-origin trust when omitted, broader access on `true`, and no exact-origin trust on `false` while retaining fake-IP DNS handling?
rationale: This determines the durable SSRF and upgrade contract for configured provider endpoints; source review can verify the implementation but cannot choose the intended security/compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve the shared three-state contract
options.body: Accept the documented exact-origin default, explicit broad opt-in, and explicit-denial semantics so this PR can proceed after normal CI and merge refresh.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in only
options.body: Change the implementation so even the configured origin remains blocked unless operators set `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true`, trading compatibility for a stricter policy.

options.title: Pause for a broader transport-policy decision
options.body: Hold this PR if memory embeddings should not share provider request policy semantics until a wider owner decision defines the cross-provider contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared three-state contract
recommendation.body: Accept the documented exact-origin default, explicit broad opt-in, and explicit-denial semantics so this PR can proceed after normal CI and merge refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the repository-wide provider transport and SSRF boundary rather than only the memory adapter.
